Subject: Terms: liability cap / indemnity / warranty — need exec concurrence

Hi Aisha,

Thanks for working through the contract with us. Our legal team reviewed the draft and has three material asks that require your leadership to sign off:

1) Liability cap: propose raising the cap to $2,000,000 (currently 1x ARR in draft).
2) Indemnity: remove the mutual carveout for customer claims tied to data processing; we need broader indemnity for third-party IP claims related to outputs.
3) Warranty: extend the warranty for the hosted service to 24 months for critical services (we understand this is atypical).

Commercial: given the above, Medidata is asking for a 25% one-time first-year discount. We have attached a marked redline of your standard SOW and a short commercial summary. Our counsel (Markus Klein) is cc'd.

These are executive-level concessions for most vendors we talk to, so please let me know the fastest path to resolution — whether you need an internal exec sign-off or a commercial counter we can accept. We are trying to get procurement complete before their board meeting on July 23.

Attachments: Medidata_redline_20240711.pdf (marked contract), Commercial_Summary_DEAL-9843.xlsx (T&Cs + pricing ask)

Subject: RE: Terms: liability cap / indemnity / warranty — legal analysis and recommended escalation

Team,

I reviewed the Medidata redline and commercial packet. Short summary and recommended escalation path below.

Summary of asks:
- Liability cap: request to move to a fixed $2,000,000 (draft currently links to 1x ARR ~ $750k).
- Indemnity: expand for third-party IP claims tied to outputs, remove certain network & processing carveouts.
- Warranty: extend from standard 90 days/limited SLA remedies to up to 24 months for certain critical modules.

Risk assessment:
- Liability cap increase materially expands tail risk; given the customer's anticipated usage patterns (heavy generative output, potential PII exposure), there's real exposure to upstream third-party claims and data incidents.
- Broadening indemnity without reciprocal limitations increases our contingent liability significantly.
- A 24-month warranty with service availability/quality promises is atypical; operationally we'd be exposed to long tail remediation costs.

Mitigation options we can propose (ranked):
1) Commercial swap: increase cap to $1.5M, accept on condition of mutual indemnity narrowing (limit to direct damages and exclude consequential; preserve narrow carveouts for open-source and customer-provided inputs). Offer a 12-month warranty for critical modules only. Commercial concession: 12% first-year discount.
2) If sales needs more commercial sweetener: $2M cap only if customer accepts higher-priced premium support agreement (adds dedicated SRE and extended monitoring) and provides indemnity for customer-supplied data. Discount capped at 15% in this path.
3) No change: keep cap tied to 1x ARR and standard indemnity/warranty. Significantly lower discount.

Action requested: this is above legal delegated approval thresholds — requires VP/SVP sign-off (commercial + legal) to proceed with 1) or 2). Please escalate to Marissa's manager/exec for authorization.

Notes: we should also insist on liability aggregation per incident, explicit sublimit for security events, and carveouts for pre-existing vulnerabilities. I'll prepare clean counters for both option 1 and 2 for signature.

-Aditya

Aditya Rao
Head of Legal Operations
Redwood Inference

Aisha / Aditya — tagging my note and ask to leadership.

Deal context: 3-year ARR estimate $750k (year 1 ~ $400k). Medidata is strategic in health vertical and reference value would be high. If we lose the board window (Jul 23), they will likely repackage and push to Q4 which increases churn risk.

Commercial view: we have room to move but need to cap downside. My preference is to pursue Aditya's option 1 as the primary path: increase cap to $1.5M, 12-month warranty for marked critical modules, and a 15% first-year discount (I can go to 15% but not 25%). If leadership pushes back, fallback is 12% + premium support upsell.

Ask for exec: VP Commercial or CRO sign-off to approve up to 15% discount + $1.5M cap with the indemnity narrowings Aditya suggested. If approved, I will authorize the clean counter and target DocuSign by EOD Mon (7/15) to meet procurement timeline.

Subject: Re: Terms: liability cap / indemnity / warranty — next steps

Carolyn — thanks for the patience. We've escalated internally and proposed two alternative paths (summarized below) so your team has options:

Option A (preferred by Legal + Sales):
- Liability cap: $1,500,000 aggregate
- Indemnity: mutual with limited carveouts; we will accept third-party IP indemnity tied to our outputs but require exclusions for open-source and customer-provided inputs; limit remedies to direct damages only
- Warranty: 12 months for the critical modules you flagged in the commercial summary
- Commercial: 15% one-time first-year discount

Option B (higher protection for Medidata):
- Liability cap: $2,000,000
- Indemnity: broader for third-party IP claims as redlined;
- Warranty: 24 months for critical modules;
- Commercial: 12% discount plus premium support add-on (separate SOW) to cover operational risk

Per our internal approvals, Option A requires approval at VP Commercial level and is within reason for a signed concession. Option B requires SVP/CRO + Head Legal exec sign-off and is only possible if Medidata accepts the premium support add-on and a clause limiting liability aggregation per incident.

Please let us know which option you prefer. If you confirm Option A, we'll circulate the clean counter for DocuSign within 24 hours. If you want Option B, we'll need to confirm the premium support scope and escalate for final sign-off (this will add an extra 48 hours).

Appreciate the urgency — we'll prioritize to meet your procurement window.

Best,
Aisha
